text:
I added `hashtags(text)` for PAY-4103 in `src/shop/hashtags.py`, with tests in `tests/test_hashtags.py`. All 13 tests pass.

The function returns unique hashtags in order of first appearance, lowercased and without the `#`. It uses the regex `(?<!\S)#(\w+)`, so a `#` counts only at the start of the text or after whitespace, and `a#b` yields nothing. Uniqueness is case-insensitive, so `#Python #python` gives `["python"]`.

Choices I made that you may want to change:
- **Module location:** a new `shop/hashtags.py`, not added to `core.py`. Import it as `from shop.hashtags import hashtags`. I did not re-export it from `shop/__init__.py`, which is empty and does not re-export `total` either.
- **Unicode:** `\w` matches letters, digits and underscores from any script, not just ASCII. If you want ASCII-only tags, switch to `re.ASCII`.
- **Tests:** the repo had no test directory, so I created `tests/`. `pytest.ini` already sets `pythonpath = src`, so the imports work as-is.
- **CHANGELOG:** added an entry under Unreleased.

pytest was not installed and the system Python blocks pip installs, so I ran the tests from a venv in `/tmp/pr2-venv-pytest`, outside the repo. The repo is not a git repository, so I did not commit anything.
prompt: Add a new feature called hashtags to this package (ticket PAY-4103). It should provide hashtags(text), returning the unique hashtags in order of first appearance, lowercase and without the '#'. A hashtag is a '#' followed by one or more letters, digits or underscores, and the '#' must be at the start of the text or right after whitespace (so 'a#b' has none). Compare case-insensitively when deciding uniqueness. Also add tests.
